name: Nikola Tesla
description: A journey through discoveries, risks, and ambitions that shaped a life of extraordinary vision — but every choice can lead you to a completely different fate.

scoring.historicalSimilarity: sum of weight for historically matching choices / sum of all event weights * 100
scoring.risk: average risk score of selected choices
scoring.independence: average independence score of selected choices

events.title: The Curious Child
events.playerFact: From the very start of your life, you possess an extraordinary ability to visualize machines in your mind. You can imagine complex inventions in full detail before ever building them. This gift both fascinates and isolates you.
events.historicalFact: You were born in 1856 in Smiljan. From an early age, you showed remarkable memory and a fascination with machines, often visualizing inventions with astonishing clarity in your mind.
events.question: You have a child who spends most of their time imagining machines. Do you encourage their unusual curiosity?

yes.consequence: You encourage the child to explore their imagination and fascination with machines.

no.consequence: You steer the child toward more conventional interests and stifle their curiosity.

events.title: Technical University
events.playerFact: You have been accepted to study electrical engineering at a prestigious technical university. This field could lead you to a deep understanding of electricity, but some friends say it's a difficult and unrewarding path.
events.historicalFact: You stulived electrical engineering at the Austrian Polytechnic in Graz and became deeply interested in the problems of electrical machines and their limitations.
events.question: Do you give up on studying electrical engineering at the university and choose another path?

yes.consequence: You abandon electrical engineering and turn to more traditional fields like civil engineering.

no.consequence: You immerse yourself in electrical engineering and begin thinking about improving electrical machines.

events.title: The Rotating Magnetic Field
events.playerFact: While walking in a city park, a complete vision comes to you: a way to run an electric motor using a rotating magnetic field instead of today's inefficient methods. The solution is so clear in your mind that you draw it in the dirt with a stick.
events.historicalFact: While working in Budapest, you conceived the idea of the rotating magnetic field — a breakthrough that would become the foundation of alternating current motors and change the world.
events.question: You suddenly imagine a completely different way to run an electric motor. Will you pursue this idea?

yes.consequence: You become obsessed with this idea and begin developing a new approach to electric motors.

no.consequence: You dismiss the idea as impractical and continue working with existing technology, never taking it seriously.

events.title: A New Country
events.playerFact: You have an opportunity to move to America and work for the most famous inventor in America. It means leaving everything you know, but America is where the future is being built.
events.historicalFact: In 1884, you moved to the United States and began working for Thomas Edison, hoping to collaborate with America's most famous inventor on electrical innovation.
events.question: Do you prefer to stay in Europe and not go to America?

yes.consequence: You stay in Europe and continue developing your ideas there, though without sufficient capital and support.

no.consequence: You leave Europe and travel to America to pursue your future in electrical engineering.

events.title: Working for the Great Inventor
events.playerFact: Your new employer prefers direct current — electricity that flows in only one direction. Your vision is alternating current, which can travel much farther. These two approaches represent fundamentally different philosophies, and your relationship gradually becomes tense.
events.historicalFact: You worked for Thomas Edison, but the two of you had fundamentally different approaches to electrical systems. Edison championed direct current, while you believed alternating current was the future.
events.question: Your employer strongly disagrees with your ideas. Will you leave and pursue your own vision?

yes.consequence: You leave your employer and decide to pursue your ideas independently.

no.consequence: You stay with the company and align your ideas with your employer's approach, though your creativity remains caged.

events.title: Alternating Current
events.playerFact: You perfect a system of alternating current that can transmit electrical power over vast distances — something direct current cannot do. You develop motors, transformers, and the entire infrastructure for a new electrical world.
events.historicalFact: You developed and patented alternating current technologies, including induction motors and polyphase systems, which made long-distance power distribution possible.
events.question: You believe alternating current can revolutionize power distribution. Will you dedicate your entire career to it?

yes.consequence: You focus on alternating current and develop technologies for large-scale power distribution.

no.consequence: You abandon the idea and turn your research elsewhere, never realizing the full potential of alternating current.

events.title: The Powerful Industrialist
events.playerFact: A powerful industrialist recognizes the potential of your electrical system and offers to license your technology and support it with his resources. This means your ideas can reach the world — but you share control.
events.historicalFact: George Westinghouse acquired the rights to your alternating current patents and provided resources to develop and deploy your technology on a massive scale.
events.question: Do you reject this partnership with the powerful industrialist to maintain your independence?

yes.consequence: You reject the partnership and try to develop the technology independently — but your funds quickly run out.

no.consequence: You allow your technology to become part of a much larger electrical system, trusting the industrialist.

events.title: The World's Fair
events.playerFact: You have the opportunity to showcase your electrical system at a world's fair — the biggest stage possible. Millions will see your technology lighting up an entire exhibition hall. It could prove once and for all that your system works.
events.historicalFact: Your alternating current system, backed by Westinghouse, illuminated the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago — a stunning public demonstration that proved AC's superiority.
events.question: You can show your electrical system to millions. Will you take this risk?

yes.consequence: You demonstrate the technology publicly, helping prove that alternating current can illuminate an entire exhibition.

no.consequence: You avoid public demonstration and keep your technology in development. Your direct current competitor takes the market.

events.title: The Remote Laboratory
events.playerFact: You become convinced that electricity can travel through the air itself — without any wires. You build a laboratory in a remote location and conduct experiments with voltages so high that lightning flashes across the plains for miles.
events.historicalFact: You conducted high-voltage experiments in Colorado Springs, producing artificial lightning and investigating wireless transmission of electrical power over distances.
events.question: Do you give up on investing in wireless experiments and turn toward more profitable technologies?

yes.consequence: You abandon the risky experiments and focus on technologies that generate reliable income — but the wireless dream never releases its hold on you.

no.consequence: You dedicate yourself to wireless electricity and high-voltage experiments, spending everything you have.

events.title: The Final Tower
events.playerFact: You have one last chance to build the dream that has consumed you: a tower that can transmit wireless power and communication across the entire world. It takes everything you have — your money, your reputation, your future. A final gamble.
events.historicalFact: You began construction of the Wardenclyffe Tower on Long Island — an ambitious facility to demonstrate wireless communication and power transmission on a global scale.
events.question: You have one last opportunity to build a system for wireless power and communication. Will you bet everything on the dream?

yes.consequence: You pour massive resources into the tower and pursue your vision of a wireless future, though you never see it completed.

no.consequence: You abandon the project before it consumes more resources and turn to more practical work, but the wireless dream haunts you for the rest of your life.

events.title: The Normal Child
events.playerFact: You suppress your child's imagination and steer them toward ordinary lessons and normal play. They grow up but never show any special talent.
events.historicalFact: History is full of unfulfilled talents who never reached their potential due to early suppression.
events.question: Do you regret stifling the child's curiosity?

yes.consequence: As the child grows up you understand his dejection, and take it as lame excuses.

no.consequence: You live peacefully, believing you did the best for your child and if he wanted to do something extraordinary he could — unaware that the world lost a genius.

events.title: A Life Without Impact
events.playerFact: Your child grows up and becomes an ordinary clerk. They never invent anything and never leave a mark.
events.historicalFact: Many families lost great talents by suppressing children's creativity.
events.question: Do you wish you had encouraged them instead of suppressing them?

yes.consequence: You are on your last leg and wish your child could find his Path

no.consequence: You live content, thinking your child had a good life — but your name is recorded in no history book.

events.title: The Structural Engineer
events.playerFact: Instead of electricity, you choose mechanical or civil engineering. You build bridges and buildings and have a quiet life, but you never approach the frontiers of electrical knowledge.
events.historicalFact: Many talented engineers of that era, by not entering emerging fields, missed great opportunities.
events.question: Are you satisfied with your traditional path?

yes.consequence: You become a successful engineer, but you never leave a lasting mark on the history of science.

no.consequence: You constantly regret missing electricity and pursue it in middle age, but it's too late.

events.title: The Unknown Bridge-Builder
events.playerFact: You have built many bridges, but the world has forgotten your name. Meanwhile, your competitors in the electrical field have achieved eternal fame.
events.historicalFact: History remembers structural engineers less than great inventors.
events.question: Do you wish you had pursued electricity instead of bridges?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had had the courage to choose the unknown path instead of security.

no.consequence: You live with pride, proud of your structures, though you know you have no place in the history of science.

events.title: A Missed Chance
events.playerFact: You do not pursue the rotating magnetic field idea. A few years later, another inventor with a similar idea transforms the world. You are merely a spectator.
events.historicalFact: The history of science is full of rivalries where an inventor, due to hesitation, lost their chance to another.
events.question: Do you feel bitter about someone else taking your place?

yes.consequence: You become bitter and live your life in the shadow of that inventor, never forgiving yourself.

no.consequence: You pass by the matter indifferently and occupy yourself with other work, but you know you lost a great opportunity.

events.title: Bitter Memories
events.playerFact: Every time you hear the name of that famous inventor, your heart sinks. You know you could have been in their place, but you weren't.
events.historicalFact: History forgets hesitant people and remembers only those who took risks.
events.question: Do you carry this regret with you forever?

yes.consequence: You live with an agonizing regret, wishing in your last breath you had chosen courage over fear.

no.consequence: You live bitterly, telling yourself it was fate — but deep down, you know it was your own fault.

events.title: The European Inventor
events.playerFact: You don't go to America and stay in Europe. You develop your ideas, but European investors are conservative and your progress is slow.
events.historicalFact: Some European inventors, despite talent, never achieved global fame due to a lack of capital and support.
events.question: Do you regret staying in Europe?

yes.consequence: Years later, when America becomes the hub of technology, you regret not going.

no.consequence: You stay in Europe with pride and continue your work, but you never become as great as your American rivals.

events.title: Unknown in Your Homeland
events.playerFact: You are known as a local inventor in Europe, but the world does not know your name. Meanwhile, your American contemporaries have achieved wealth and fame.
events.historicalFact: The history of technology records Europe as the second stage during that period.
events.question: Do you wish you had gone to America?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had had the courage to travel and take risks.

no.consequence: You live peacefully, telling yourself you preferred your homeland over fame — though you know your impact on history is small.

events.title: Following the Boss
events.playerFact: You stay with your employer and set aside your ideas. You work on direct current, even though you know it is limited. You spend years in his shadow.
events.historicalFact: Some of Edison's colleagues, despite talent, remained in his shadow and never achieved self-realization.
events.question: Do you regret this forced alignment?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had had the courage to stand up instead of obeying.

no.consequence: You live peacefully, believing that collaborating with your employer was the wise choice, though you never reached the peak.

events.title: The Unknown Associate
events.playerFact: Alongside your employer, you achieve some success, but you always remain in his shadow. Your name is not recorded in history alongside his.
events.historicalFact: History remembers associates less than leaders.
events.question: Do you wish you had gone your own way?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had pursued your own vision instead of aligning with your boss.

no.consequence: You live with pride, proud to have worked alongside a genius, even though you never became one yourself.

events.title: Wandering Through Technology
events.playerFact: You abandon alternating current and turn to various scattered projects. You never go deep, and you never make a great invention.
events.historicalFact: Many inventors, through scattered efforts, never created lasting work.
events.question: Do you regret this scattering?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had focused on one big idea instead of many incomplete ones.

no.consequence: You live peacefully, believing variety made your life interesting, though you added nothing important to the world.

events.title: The Forgotten Inventor
events.playerFact: You have registered small, unrelated inventions, but none of them changed the world. In the archives of history, your name is lost among thousands of unknown inventors.
events.historicalFact: The history of technology is a graveyard of incomplete ideas.
events.question: Do you wish you had focused on one idea?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had had the courage to focus instead of scattering your efforts.

no.consequence: You live content, believing your varied life was valuable — unaware that the world never felt your impact.

events.title: Alone Against the Giants
events.playerFact: You reject the industrialist's partnership and try to commercialize your technology yourself. But your funds quickly run out, and your competitors, with strong financial backing, seize the market.
events.historicalFact: The history of entrepreneurship is full of those who failed due to lacking a powerful partner.
events.question: Do you regret this decision?

yes.consequence: With bankruptcy, you lose everything. Years later, you regret turning down the powerful partner.

no.consequence: Despite the failure, you don't blame yourself, believing independence was more valuable than any partnership — even though it led to ruin.

events.title: The Fall
events.playerFact: You have nothing left. Your inventions are in others' hands, and you live in poverty. Once you could have changed the world, but now you are just a memory of a brilliant past.
events.historicalFact: History has seen inventors who, due to poor financial management, fell from the peak to the bottom.
events.question: Do you wish you had chosen partnership over independence?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had thought about sustainability instead of pride.

no.consequence: You live with pride, believing you maintained your independence even in failure — though the world does not remember you.

events.title: Secrecy
events.playerFact: You refuse to publicly demonstrate your technology. Your direct current competitor lights up the fair, and the world considers them the winner. Your technology is never seen.
events.historicalFact: Some inventors, due to fear of idea theft, never properly introduced their work, and history passed them by.
events.question: Do you regret this secrecy?

yes.consequence: Years later, when alternating current becomes widespread but under another name, you regret not stepping forward.

no.consequence: You never make your technology public and live in isolation, while the world never knows who you were.

events.title: The Hidden Treasure
events.playerFact: You have hidden your inventions in drawers and never shown them to anyone. When you live, you take them to the grave, and the world never learns of their existence.
events.historicalFact: The history of science is full of unknown ideas that were never seen.
events.question: Do you wish you had shown them to the world?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had had the courage to share instead of hiding.

no.consequence: You live peacefully, believing your ideas live with you — but you know the world lost something it will never find.

events.title: The Merchant of Science
events.playerFact: You abandon wireless experiments and move toward more profitable technologies. You become wealthy but never achieve the wireless dream.
events.historicalFact: Some inventors chose immediate profitability over great dreams and never reached profound depths.
events.question: Do you regret this practical choice?

yes.consequence: You live wealthy but with an empty heart, always wishing you had continued those experiments.

no.consequence: You live satisfied with your wealth, believing rationality is better than dreaming — but you know you never came close to the frontiers of knowledge.

events.title: Rich but Forgotten
events.playerFact: You have great wealth, but there is no mention of you in the history of science. Your wireless dream was never realized, and the world remembers you as a businessman, not an inventor.
events.historicalFact: History remembers the wealthy less than the discoverers.
events.question: Was wealth worth the loss of the dream?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had pursued your dreams instead of money.

no.consequence: You live with pride, proud of your wealth, but deep down you know the world will never remember you.

events.title: زندگی بی‌اثر
events.playerFact: After talking to your dad, You make effort work round the clock to get to success but It is a farfetched goal
events.historicalFact: بسیاری از خانواده‌ها با سرکوب خلاقیت کودکان، استعدادهای بزرگ را از دست دادند.
events.question: Would you give up by facing the other's success while for you every thing was steady?

yes.consequence: Give up and make your Earning to live like before.

no.consequence: Although you are aged, but the Progress is too slow.
